name: Red Bull Ring

sources.geometry: OpenStreetMap highway=raceway ways (Overpass API, (c) OSM contributors, ODbL); station 0 on OSM node "Finish Line" (control/timing line; the separate "Start Line" is ~120 m further on).
sources.width: Measured on basemap.at orthophoto 30 cm (bmaporthofoto30cm, z19 WMTS, https://basemap.at) by detecting edge-line/kerb pairs on perpendicular profiles every 12 m (~60% of samples), gaps interpolated, clipped 10.5-16 m.
sources.elevation: BEV ALS DTM 1 m (Digitales Gelaendemodell aus Airborne Laserscanning, data.bev.gv.at tile CRS3035RES50000mN2650000E4650000, ref. date 2019-09-15, CC BY 4.0), heights above Adriatic datum; centre samples every 3 m, ~15 m smoothing.
sources.camber: BEV ALS DTM 1 m: crossfall from edge samples 1.2 m inside each edge vs centre (every 6 m), smoothed.
sources.pit: OSM way "Boxenstrasse" (Pit Lane), entry before Turn 10, exit after Turn 1.
sources.trim: Medium-downforce track, similar level to Spa: long uphill straights vs. slow T1/T3/T4 and fast T6-T10.
sources.pitLimit: F1 pit lane speed limit 80 km/h (FIA Event Notes, Austrian GP).
sources.pitLoss: Computed from Jolpica/Ergast lap times (in-lap + out-lap - 2 x median clean lap): median 20.8 s (2024), 21.0 s (2025), 21.4 s (2026); includes the ~2.5 s stationary time.
sources.raceLaps: 2026 Austrian GP (round 8, 28 Jun 2026): 71 laps, not a sprint weekend (F1 2026 sprint calendar).

notes: Official F1 lap length 4.318 km (circuit now quotes 4.326 km measured by the newer FIA centre-line method). Corner names follow the circuit (T3 Remus/Interwetten, T4 Rauch, T7 Graz, T9 Jochen Rindt); OSM still carries older sponsor names. ~65 m elevation range, max climb ~12% to Remus.
